parts.title: My first camping trip
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my school organised a camping trip for our class, and I was terrified. I had never slept outside before, and I am not the kind of person who enjoys insects. My best friend, Daria, was more excited than I was. She had packed a torch, three jumpers and enough biscuits for the whole group.

We arrived at the campsite on a Friday afternoon. The teachers divided us into groups of four, and we had to put up our own tent. It sounded easy, but it took us nearly an hour, because one of the poles was broken and the instructions were missing. When we finally finished, the tent was a little crooked, but it was standing.

That evening we cooked sausages on a fire and told stories. It was the first time I had seen so many stars. I tried to count them, but I gave up after about fifty. Later, at night, the weather changed, and it started to rain heavily. Daria found out that our tent was not completely waterproof when a drop landed on her nose. We moved our sleeping bags to the middle and laughed until morning.

On Saturday we were tired, wet and happy. Our teacher told us that the crooked tent had a prize for being the most creative. I still do not like insects, but I now understand why people enjoy camping. I am already planning to ask my parents if we can go together this summer.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel before the trip?
questions.explanation: She says she was terrified because she had never slept outside and does not like insects.

questions.prompt: Why did it take so long to put up the tent?
options: A pole was broken and there were no instructions.
They did not know how to start it properly.
They had no teacher to help them at all.
questions.explanation: One of the poles was broken and the instructions were missing, so it took nearly an hour.

questions.prompt: What did the writer enjoy on Friday evening?
questions.explanation: She saw many stars and tried to count them.

questions.prompt: What happened in the night?
questions.explanation: A drop of rain landed on Daria's nose, showing that the tent was not completely waterproof.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel at the end of the trip?
options: She was too tired to speak.
questions.explanation: She understands why people enjoy camping and wants to ask her parents to go together.

parts.title: A school in the forest
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
At the edge of a forest in the north of England, a group of children is learning how to light a fire. They are not at school in the usual way, but at a forest school, where children spend most of their lessons outdoors, whatever the weather. [1] Teachers say that this makes children more confident.

A typical day begins with a walk to the clearing, where the group has a base. [2] They use sticks, ropes and old blankets to make a shelter, and in winter they sit round the fire to drink hot chocolate.

The children also learn about nature. They collect leaves, look for insects and listen to the birds. [3] Some of them can now tell the difference between twenty kinds of tree.

Many parents were worried about safety at first. [4] Children learn to use tools carefully, and an adult is always with them. Accidents are rare.

Not every child loves it immediately. [5] "At first, I hated the mud," says nine-year-old Nell. "Now I'd be sad if it was ever sunny."
sentences: Some of them are shy at the start and find the cold and the mud difficult.
However, the forest is not a rough or dangerous place, because the rules are very clear.
Their parents come to watch on Friday afternoons.
Rain, wind and snow are all part of the lesson.
First, the children decide what they want to do that day.
After a few months, they know the names of most of the plants around them.

gaps.explanation: "Whatever the weather" leads to rain, wind and snow being part of the lesson; "this" in the next sentence refers to learning outdoors in all weather.
After the walk to the clearing, the children first decide what to do; the next sentence says what they use to build a shelter.
They collect leaves and listen to birds, and after a few months they know the plants; the next sentence says they can name twenty kinds of tree.
Parents were worried about safety, and "However" shows that the forest is not dangerous; the next sentences explain how tools are used carefully.
"Not every child loves it immediately" is followed by the shy children who find the cold and mud difficult, which matches Nell's comment about mud.

parts.title: Staying safe on a hike
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Going for a long walk in the mountains is a wonderful way to enjoy nature, but you must [1] carefully before you leave. Always check the weather forecast, because conditions can [2] very quickly at high altitude. Wear strong boots and carry a waterproof jacket, even if the sky is blue. You should also take plenty of water and some food, [3] you may feel tired on the way back. It is a good idea to tell someone [4] you are going and when you expect to return. If you get lost, stay where you are, because walking [5] the dark is dangerous, and call for help. Finally, remember to [6] your phone fully charged.

parts.title: Getting ready for camping
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Wyn,
I am so excited about our camping trip on Saturday! I have already packed my sleeping bag, [1] I still need to buy a new torch. My brother says we should take warm clothes, [2] it can get very cold at night, even in summer. Do you know [3] to put up the tent? If not, I will show you. We are going to cook sausages on a small stove, so do not forget to bring a plate [4] a fork. I [5] never been to this campsite, but I have heard that it is next to a lake. I hope the weather stays dry [6] the whole weekend!
Pieter

gaps.explanation: "But" contrasts what he has done with what he still needs to do.
"Because" gives the reason for taking warm clothes.
"Do you know how to put up the tent?" asks about the method.
"And" joins the plate and the fork.
The present perfect "have never been" talks about his experience.
"For the whole weekend" says how long.

parts.title: A guide talks about a nature walk
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to Lake Meadow Nature Park. My name's Marietta, and I'll be your guide today. We're going to follow the Heron Trail, which is about six kilometres long. We'll start here at the visitor centre and walk round the lake. Along the way, you might see squirrels in the trees and perhaps a deer if we are quiet. The walk takes about three hours, with a break for lunch at the picnic area. Please wear strong shoes, because some parts of the path can be muddy. The walk is free, but if you would like to give money to help the park, there's a box by the door. Does anybody have any questions before we begin?

parts.title: An interview with a mountain guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Rosalba, you have been a mountain guide for twenty years. What do you enjoy most about it?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Being outdoors every day, of course, but mostly watching other people succeed. When someone who thought they could never climb reaches the top, it is the best moment of my job.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the most important piece of equipment?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: People think it is the rope or the helmet, but it is a good pair of boots. If your feet hurt, you cannot enjoy anything else. I always tell my groups to wear their boots for a few weeks before the trip.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What mistakes do beginners often make?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: They try to go too fast at the start. They are full of energy, and after an hour they are exhausted. Slow and steady wins on a mountain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Have you ever been in danger?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Once. A sudden storm came in while we were above the clouds, and we had to wait for three hours in a small shelter. Everyone was frightened, but we stayed calm and nobody was hurt. It taught me always to carry extra food and warm clothes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How has the job changed?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: There are many more visitors than there used to be, and some of them leave rubbish on the paths. I now spend part of my time teaching people to look after the mountains.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is your advice to somebody who wants to start?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Begin with short walks near home and listen to experienced people. You do not have to climb big peaks to enjoy being in nature.
